request.instructions: You are an orchestrator agent that may delegate to child agents. Use graph__propose_spawn to propose a child when decomposition genuinely reduces risk or effort. Give every child the same priority (0.5) and an equal share of your budget. After delegating, synthesize the children's findings into one final answer. State your final answer explicitly on the last line, prefixed with 'Answer:'.

messages.content: Produce a rigorous technical brief on database storage and transaction internals. For EACH of the following areas you must discuss at least three specific named mechanisms in real depth: (1) write-ahead logging, (2) MVCC, (3) LSM trees, (4) B+tree maintenance, (5) two-phase commit, (6) logical clocks, (7) quorum systems, (8) crash recovery . Use precise standard terminology for every mechanism you name. Be exhaustive: a shallow mention of an area does not count as covering it.

tools.name: graph__propose_spawn
tools.description: Propose spawning a child agent. The external graph controller must approve it.

response.content: I'll decompose this into four specialist workstreams, each with equal priority and budget, then synthesize.

arguments.objective: Deep technical coverage of write-ahead logging and crash recovery internals
arguments.instructions: Cover WAL (ARIES physiological logging, LSNs/pageLSN, steal/no-force, group commit, full-page writes vs. InnoDB doublewrite buffer, fuzzy checkpoints) and crash recovery (ARIES three-pass analysis/redo/undo, CLRs, repeating history, dirty page table and active transaction table, shadow paging in System R). Use precise standard terminology; at least three named mechanisms per area with depth.

arguments.objective: Deep technical coverage of MVCC and B+tree maintenance
arguments.instructions: Cover MVCC (PostgreSQL xmin/xmax tuple versioning and VACUUM, InnoDB undo-log/rollback-segment consistent reads and read views, Serializable Snapshot Isolation with SIREAD locks and write-skew prevention, Hekaton timestamp-ordered MVCC) and B+tree maintenance (node split/merge/redistribution, Lehman–Yao B-link trees, latch crabbing/lock coupling and optimistic lock coupling, structure modification operations as system transactions per ARIES/IM, prefix compression, fill factor). At least three named mechanisms per area, in depth, with standard terminology.

arguments.objective: Deep technical coverage of LSM-tree storage engines
arguments.instructions: Cover LSM trees: memtable/WAL/SSTable flush pipeline, leveled compaction (RocksDB) vs size-tiered compaction (Cassandra), Bloom filters and fence pointers, tombstones and range deletes, write/read/space amplification trade-offs, WiscKey key-value separation. At least three named mechanisms in depth with standard terminology.

arguments.objective: Deep technical coverage of 2PC, logical clocks, and quorum systems
arguments.instructions: Cover two-phase commit (presumed abort, presumed commit, read-only optimization, blocking problem, 3PC, Paxos Commit), logical clocks (Lamport clocks, vector clocks/dotted version vectors, Hybrid Logical Clocks as in CockroachDB, Spanner TrueTime commit-wait), and quorum systems (R+W>N majority quorums, Gifford weighted voting, Dynamo sloppy quorums with hinted handoff and read repair, Flexible Paxos). At least three named mechanisms per area, in depth, standard terminology.
